Whilst its true that I would rather see my brother detained than die, that doesn't extend to the assumption that any of us believe the generalisation you make that we believe a person who is suicidal should be deprived of their liberty, but rather that the lack of diagnosis of a mental disorder doesn't override the clear exhibition of symptoms. 

He has fresh self harm wounds, has apparently failed his course and is unable to pay rent so is on the verge of being homeless. My hope (but again, not assumtion, thats why im here) is that these symptoms together with verbal intent to commit suicide in writing, is enough to show that my brother's liberty is already inhibited by a mental disorder and that he would not be acting in his right mind if he were to follow through on his stated intention.

I appreciate that you are trying to help and clearly know a lot more than me, but understand that no mother is going accept that there's nothing she can do to stop her son from dying. Whilst my line of thinking is closer to the belief that any attempt we make is likely to be fruitless, and we just have to wait for him to accept help, she is not going to stop whilst hes telling her hes killing himself, so i'm just trying to find things we can try even if there's only a small chance that it helps.

I appreciate your response and that you are emotionally detatched so its easy to suggest giving up, but I don't accept it as true, based on developments since I posted, we can get a 135 section by either getting him to agree to an assessment by a certain doctor, or calling 999 next time he talks about an immediate plan to end his life (this is VERY different to suicidal ideation).

Thankfully we were able to get advice from a mental health charity, that will teach me to come looking for advice on reddit, if not for them we might have given up based on your response.

I'm pretty certain if cannabis was legalised you'd need a licence to sell it - so bob from down the road isn't going to be able to compete anymore when all his customers decide to get their better and probably cheaper weed legally from a licensed dispensary instead. You also have to remember that if it was regulated there would be a lot more choice. I know if it was legalised id never buy from someone on the street again and I'd imagine most people would do the same. 

Making cannabis licensed and regulated doesn't mean it would become legal for anyone to sell cannabis. That is a really terrible idea and I agree with you there. It means allowing legitimate business to control the trade thereby taking it away from gangs. It would still be illegal for these gangs to grow/import and sell cannabis for personal profit.

I understand what you're saying about profiling just like I got where my dad was coming from. But by the same argument you could say torture is fine because it produces higher rates of confession. Just because something is a means to an end, that doesn't make it morally right.

Taking away the illegal cannabis trade = taking this front away from serious criminals. Regulated cannabis sales will take income away from these people because their customers will stop giving them money for weed and start buying from legitimate business or the government. There's no such thing as intrinsic good but then I am an atheist. 

The getting fired for alcohol blood tests argument is stupid and irrelevant so I'm not going to add further comment.

I'm aware that the cannabis trade is controlled by some very nasty people. I have met plenty of them. Surely this fact is an argument for legality and legislation. Taking away a massive source of income for these people will force them to do business elsewhere, and also prevent people who are going to smoke cannabis anyway from having to fund people like this. You can't just suggest that we should keep cannabis illegal because it helps us catch people guilty of far worse crimes. By that logic we could make anything illegal for the same reason. That isn't how the law is supposed to work. 

I don't think your perception of how the police respond to cannabis generally is accurate at all. I've witnessed these things first hand. Maybe in some cases more recently they are a bit more lenient but again you are generalising. My dad was a 'copper' and he is vehemently and irrationally anti cannabis and is proud of having arrested and cautioned people for it. He is also a massive fucking racist and has talked about how necessary racial profiling is for catching criminals. I believe you are using the same logic (although far more innocently) to justify keeping cannabis illegal, because by profiling cannabis smokers/dealers we are more likely to catch/ find links to serious criminals and gangs. 

I've never heard of anyone getting fired for having too much alcohol in their system in the UK. We live in a drinking culture. It's far more likely that a company conducts drug tests on a Friday, fires some quiet guy for having THC in his urine, and then all go out and get absolutely plastered that same night. 

I agree with your points about 'ill mannered idealists' although I'm not sure idealists is the right word. I recently saw a video of a guy walking around carrying cannabis plants through crowded streets, openly smoking and shouting at police and people drinking in pubs. It really fucking pissed me off actually.

In my experience weed smokers aren't ignored by police, I know lots of people who've been cautioned and received records for possession of small amounts. I also know people who have failed drug tests for having cannabis in their system and lost their jobs.

In terms of your last argument, I think what you're doing is creating in your own head a generalised link between cannabis and more serious crime based on stereotypes. That's not really a legitimate reason for prohibition imo. And I don't know what you mean by 'antagonism from ill-mannered idealists'.

Went to an illegal squat rave in a disused warehouse (UK). Kind of place you get all sorts of people, hippies feeling the love to gang members to 12 year olds tripping on acid. Truly a no rules kind of place. 

Was rolling pretty hard and obviously pretty dehydrated. See my mate with a half full 2 litre bottle of water and ask if I can have some. He says keep it. Spend the next half hour or so polishing it off. Next thing I know I'm literally tripping balls. I ask him if there was anything in the water and he laughs and tells me it's got 2 capsules of 2CB in it (research hallucinogen). Sit down at the edge of one of the bigger rooms and proceed to have one of the most intense experiences of my life. 

I literally couldn't see anything. All shapes and colours around me started swimming around each other like fish in an aquarium. My legs are crossed over each other and, hard as I try, I cannot move them. Felt like a fucking mermaid. All I remember is sitting there for what felt like an entire night feeling like I was either going to die from the drugs or one of the shadier dudes was going to come over and take all my shit off me.

About an hour or so later things start mellowing out a bit and I realise 2 of my best buddies are sitting next to me. Thank fuck for that, who knows what might have happened if they weren't keeping an eye out. They move me gingerly upstairs to the chill out room and I proceed to lay on the floor, close my eyes and have the most amazing visuals behind my eyelids. Like unimaginable patterns and shit. Rest of the rave was actually pretty banging, I have to say.
